\section[\texorpdfstring{\te{కాపాడు} (kāpāḍu)}{కాపాడు (kāpāḍu)}]{\te{కాపాడు} (kāpāḍu) — to protect, to save}

\label{lesson:TE-C148-kapadu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for to win, then the Telugu for to hide.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{కాపాడు}}
\textbf{\te{కాపాడు}} — \emph{kāpāḍu} — \textquotedblleft{}to protect, to save\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\te{కాపాడు}} (\emph{kāpāḍu}) is native Dravidian. DEDR 1416 lists \emph{kāpāḍu}, \textquotedblleft{}to protect, save\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{kācu}, \textquotedblleft{}to guard\textquotedblright{}, with Tamil \emph{kā}, \textquotedblleft{}to guard\textquotedblright{}. DEDR compares Prakrit \emph{kāhila}, \textquotedblleft{}cowherd\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāpāḍu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāpāḍu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{kāpāḍu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for to win, then the Telugu for to hide, then say \emph{kāpāḍu} again
\end{itemize}
